SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 6
SUBJECT: SCIENCE & TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water always increases oxygen
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

2. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Movement of water only across a membrane
   B. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   C. Heating until a solid melts
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Composition of Air? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Composition of Air.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Composition of Air.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Composition of Air.

4. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Levers as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Levers as simple machines.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Levers as simple machines.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Levers as simple machines.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Invertebrates? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Invertebrates.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Invertebrates.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Invertebrates.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

7. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Only carbon dioxide
   D. Nitrogen gas only

8. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Milk souring
   B. Paper burning to ash
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Slopes as simple machines? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Slopes as simple machines.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Slopes as simple machines.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Slopes as simple machines.

10. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Burning crop residue every week
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Removing all vegetation
   D. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. newton (N)
   B. watt (W)
   C. joule (J)
   D. pascal (Pa)

12. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   B. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   C. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   D. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Light and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Levers as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Slopes as simple machines and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Invertebrates and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. B — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

2. B — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

3. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Composition of Air.

4. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Levers as simple machines.

5. D — 100 °C

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Invertebrates.

7. B — Glucose and oxygen

8. C — Ice melting to water

9. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Slopes as simple machines.

10. D — Planting cover crops and terracing slopes

11. A — newton (N)

12. D — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Light; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Levers as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Slopes as simple machines; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Invertebrates; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
